backlogged.summary: When base_timed_out is set the verify output gives no warning line, so a reviewer cannot notice that vacuity was not actually checked (same concern as open backlog B242).
The F33 AC-3 test takes about 24 s and the SC-1 test about 11 s because of real wall-clock sleeps. On a loaded CI host these could flake or slow the suite.

A base check that really passes on base but runs longer than vacuity_timeout_sec is counted as non-vacuous, and verify prints no warning when base_timed_out is set. A reviewer can only see it by reading the criterion entry.

A base vacuity run that is aborted (run signal) rather than timed out is neither base_timed_out nor vacuous, so it silently counts as non-vacuous. This behaviour existed before F33, but it is the same 'did not pass on base' asymmetry and is not documented in SPEC §6.3.
The SC-1 test checks that the child process is gone and the worktree is removed only on POSIX (process group kill). The Windows taskkill /T path for a timed-out base run has no test.
